## Make a scatter plot with fitted line

::: nonincremental

- Using `geom_point()` plots the scatter plot of the raw data.
- Adding the layer `geom_smooth(method="lm")` plots a line using a straight line, AKA linear model ("lm" stands for "linear model").

:::

The dependent variable is `score`, the independent variable is `time`, and the dataset name is "raw_data". How would create scatter plot with a fitted line?

:::: code-puzzle
::: static
ggplot({{{raw_data}}}, aes(x={{time}}, y={{score}})) + {{geom_point()}} + {{geom_smooth(method="lm")}}
:::
::::


## Fit a linear model

::: nonincremental

The `lm()` function in R helps us fit a linear model through our data ("lm" stands for "linear model"). It works like this:

- lm(dependent_variable ~ independent_variable, data=data_name)
- Then use `%>%` to apply the function `summary()`. Doing so will output more information about the model you fitted.

The dependent variable is `score`, the independent variable is `time`, and the dataset name is "raw_data". How would you fit a linear model?
:::

:::: code-puzzle
::: static

lm({{score}} ~ {{time}}, data = {{raw_data}}) %>% {{summary()}}

:::
::::

:::::
